proposals.before: Third month, wuwu new moon: Prince of Dingguo Gong died.
proposals.after: Third month, wuwu new moon: Gong, Prince of Dingguo, died.
proposals.reason: 栱 is the personal name; Dingguo is the princely fief, not a fused compound name.

proposals.before: Day yisi: Zhong Hu, military commissioner of Dingguo Army, was made Grand Mentor with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies.
proposals.after: Day yisi: Zhong Hu, military commissioner of Dingguo Army, was granted kaifu yitong sansi, ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies.
proposals.reason: 開府儀同三司 is not the office of Grand Mentor.

proposals.before: Zhenghe year 3, spring, first month, day jiwei: the Prince of Ding, Wang Huan, and the Prince of Jia, Wang Kai, were both made Grand Guardian.
proposals.after: Zhenghe year 3, spring, first month, day jiwei: the Prince of Ding, Huan, and the Prince of Jia, Kai, were both made Grand Guardian.
proposals.reason: 王 in 定王桓 and 嘉王楷 is the princely title, not the surname Wang.

proposals.before: On bingyin, Prince of Yan Wang You became Grand Tutor.
proposals.after: On bingyin, Yu, Prince of Yan, became Grand Tutor.
proposals.reason: 燕王俁 is Yu; 王 is the princely title, not a surname, and You mistranslates 俁.

proposals.before: Day bingyin: the Prince of Yan, Wang You, was made Grand Tutor.
proposals.after: Day bingyin: the Prince of Yan, Yu, was made Grand Tutor.
proposals.reason: 俁 is Yu, not You; 王 is title not surname.

proposals.before: Day jimao: the Prince of Yue, Wang Si, was made Grand Tutor; son Jian was enfeoffed Duke of Hanguo.
proposals.after: Day jimao: the Prince of Yue, Si, was made Grand Tutor; son Jian was enfeoffed Duke of Hanguo.
proposals.reason: 王 in 越王偲 is the princely title, not the surname Wang.

proposals.before: On gengyin, recovery of Qin, Bo, and the rest won a grace decree in Zi-Cui.
proposals.after: On gengyin, recovery of Qin, Bo, and the rest won a grace decree in Zi-Kui.
proposals.reason: 夔 is Kui, not Cui; Zi-Cui misreads 梓夔路.

proposals.before: Day renwu: the Imperial Temple was feasted; Emperor Shenzong's posthumous title was extended to Emperor Tiyuan Xiandao Fagu Lixian Dide Wanggong Yingwen Liewu Qinren Shengsiao; Emperor Zhezong's was changed to Emperor Xianyuan Jidao Shide Yanggong Qinwen Ruiwu Qisheng Zhaoxiao.
proposals.after: Day renwu: the Imperial Temple was feasted; Emperor Shenzong's posthumous title was extended to Emperor Tiyuan Xiandao Fagu Lixian Dide Wanggong Yingwen Liewu Qinren Shengxiao; Emperor Zhezong's was changed to Emperor Xianyuan Jidao Shide Yanggong Qinwen Ruiwu Qisheng Zhaoxiao.
proposals.reason: 聖孝 is Shengxiao; Shengsiao is a corrupted romanization.

proposals.before: Fourth month, gengxu: at the Secretariat he admonished Cai Jing and He Zhizhong by autograph, advanced their ranks, and gave clerks graded gifts of silk.
proposals.after: Fourth month, gengxu: at the Department of State Affairs he admonished Cai Jing and He Zhizhong by autograph, advanced their ranks, and gave clerks graded gifts of silk.
proposals.reason: 尚書省 is the Department of State Affairs, not the Secretariat (中書省).

proposals.before: Summer, fourth month, day gengxu: the emperor visited the Secretariat; by handwritten edict he admonished Cai Jing and He Zhizhong; each was advanced in rank and clerks were given silk in graded amounts.
proposals.after: Summer, fourth month, day gengxu: the emperor visited the Department of State Affairs; by handwritten edict he admonished Cai Jing and He Zhizhong; each was advanced in rank and clerks were given silk in graded amounts.
proposals.reason: 尚書省 is the Department of State Affairs, not the Secretariat.

proposals.before: Second month, yisi: Prince of Ding Huan was made heir apparent.
proposals.after: Second month, yisi: Huan, Prince of Ding, was made heir apparent.
proposals.reason: English fuses the title 定王 with the given name 桓 as if Ding Huan were a compound personal name.

proposals.before: Second month, day yisi: Prince of Ding Huan was established as heir apparent.
proposals.after: Second month, day yisi: Huan, Prince of Ding, was established as heir apparent.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise treats 定王桓 as Prince of Ding Huan instead of Huan, Prince of Ding.

proposals.before: Heir of the Prince of Pu Zhongzeng died.
proposals.after: Zhongzeng, Heir of the Prince of Pu, died.
proposals.reason: English runs the title 嗣濮王 into the personal name 仲增, as if Pu Zhongzeng were a single name.

proposals.before: Heir of the Prince of Pu Zhongzeng died.
proposals.after: Zhongzeng, Heir of the Prince of Pu, died.
proposals.reason: Literal English has the same fused title-plus-name as the idiomatic line.

proposals.before: On bingxu, the son Huan was enfeoffed Duke of Hui.
proposals.after: On bingxu, the son Ying was enfeoffed Duke of Hui.
proposals.reason: 楧 is not the same name as 桓 (Huan) in s0133; the given name should be Ying.

proposals.before: Day bingxu: the son Huan was enfeoffed Duke of Hui.
proposals.after: Day bingxu: the son Ying was enfeoffed Duke of Hui.
proposals.reason: Literal English repeats the wrong romanization Huan for 楧.

proposals.before: Eleventh month, dingchou: the son Chan was enfeoffed Duke of Xiang.
proposals.after: Eleventh month, dingchou: the son Chan was enfeoffed Duke of Xiangguo.
proposals.reason: 相國公 is Duke of Xiangguo, not a shortened Duke of Xiang that drops 國.

proposals.before: On gengzi, Zheng Juzhong became junior guardian and chancellery vice director; Liu Zhengfu became special advanced and secretariat vice director.
proposals.after: On gengzi, Zheng Juzhong became Junior Guardian, Grand Chancellor, and Vice Director of the Chancellery; Liu Zhengfu became Special Advanced, Junior Chancellor, and Vice Director of the Secretariat.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English omits 太宰 (Grand Chancellor) and 少宰 (Junior Chancellor), which the Chinese and literal fields both record.

proposals.before: On wuzi, Zongcu became Grandee of the Palace.
proposals.after: On wuzi, Zongcui became Grandee of the Palace.
proposals.reason: 宗粹 is Zongcui; Zongcu drops the final syllable of 粹.

proposals.before: On xinwei, He Zhizhong retired as Grand Preceptor but attended on new and full moons.
proposals.after: On xinwei, He Zhizhong was made Grand Preceptor and retired, attending court on the new and full moons.
proposals.reason: 為太傅致仕 is a grant of Grand Preceptor upon retirement, not merely retiring from that office; 朝朔望 is attendance on the first and fifteenth.

proposals.before: Seventh month, renchen: Xinghe, Huancqing, and Jingyuan were shaken by earthquake.
proposals.after: Seventh month, renchen: Xinghe, Huanqing, and Jingyuan were shaken by earthquake.
proposals.reason: Huancqing is a misspelling of Huanqing for 環慶; the fused extra c is not a place name.

proposals.before: Autumn, seventh month, day renchen: Xinghe, Huancqing, and Jingyuan circuits were shaken by earthquake.
proposals.after: Autumn, seventh month, day renchen: Xinghe, Huanqing, and Jingyuan circuits were shaken by earthquake.
proposals.reason: Literal English repeats the same Huancqing misspelling of 環慶 (Huanqing).

proposals.before: On wuchen, Prince of Jia Kai became Grand Tutor.
proposals.after: On wuchen, Kai, Prince of Jia, became Grand Tutor.
proposals.reason: 嘉王楷 is Kai, the Prince of Jia, not a person named Jia Kai; the English fuses the title and given name.

proposals.before: Day wuchen: Prince of Jia Kai was made Grand Tutor.
proposals.after: Day wuchen: Kai, Prince of Jia, was made Grand Tutor.
proposals.reason: Same fused rendering of 嘉王楷 as Jia Kai rather than given name Kai with title Prince of Jia.

proposals.before: Military commissioner observation retainers became commissioner envoys.
proposals.after: Military-commissioner and observation-commissioner retainers were renamed commissioners for proclaiming orders.
proposals.reason: 節度觀察留後 are the retainer posts of jiedushi and guanchashi, retitled 承宣使; the English collapses the offices into an opaque phrase.

proposals.before: On dingmao, Kai was advanced to Prince of Yan.
proposals.after: On dingmao, Kai was advanced to Prince of Yun.
proposals.reason: 鄆 is Yun (Yunzhou), not Yan; Yan would be 兗/燕. The promotion is to Prince of Yun.

proposals.before: Day dingmao: Kai was advanced to Prince of Yan.
proposals.after: Day dingmao: Kai was advanced to Prince of Yun.
proposals.reason: 鄆王 is Prince of Yun, not Yan.

proposals.before: The Chai heir already held Chongyi; the former Zhou empress was made Xuanyi lang to tend the Zhou tombs, with perpetual three courtesies.
proposals.after: The Chai heir already held Chongyi; a descendant of Emperor Gong was again established as Xuanyi lang to tend the Zhou tombs, with perpetual three courtesies.
proposals.reason: 恭帝后 here means the posterity of Later Zhou Emperor Gong, not a former empress; 宣義郎 is a male civil title.

proposals.before: An edict: a Zhou Chai clan descendant had already been enfeoffed Duke of Chongyi; the former empress was reestablished as Lang of Xuanyi to supervise Zhou imperial tombs, with perpetual three courtesies toward the state.
proposals.after: An edict: a Zhou Chai clan descendant had already been enfeoffed Duke of Chongyi; a descendant of Emperor Gong was again established as Lang of Xuanyi to supervise Zhou imperial tombs, with perpetual three courtesies toward the state.
proposals.reason: 恭帝后 is the descendant line of Emperor Gong, not an empress.

proposals.before: On xinyou, heterodox memorialist An Yaochén received office.
proposals.after: On xinyou, the memorialist An Yaochen received office.
proposals.reason: 上書人 means a person who submitted a memorial, not necessarily a heterodox writer; the accented spelling is unnecessary.

decisions.after: Third month, wuwu new moon: Gong, Duke of Dingguo, died.
decisions.reason: 定國公栱 names Gong, a duke of Dingguo: 栱 is the given name and 公 is duke, not prince. The proposal unfused the name but still rendered 公 as Prince.
開府儀同三司 is a prestige rank with Three Excellencies ceremony, not the office of Grand Mentor (太傅).

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以定國軍節度使仲忽為開府儀同三司

decisions.reason: 定王桓 and 嘉王楷 use 王 as the princely title, not the surname Wang; the given names are Huan and Kai.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以定王桓、嘉王楷並為太保

decisions.reason: 燕王俁 is Yu, Prince of Yan: 王 is the title and 俁 is Yu, not the surname-plus-name Wang You.
燕王俁 is the Prince of Yan, Yu; 俁 is not You and 王 is not a surname.
越王偲 uses 王 as the princely title; the given name is Si, not the surname Wang.

decisions.after: On gengyin, recovery of Zhen, Bo, and the rest won a grace decree in Zi-Kui.
decisions.reason: 梓夔路 is Zi-Kui (夔, not Cui). The proposal left 溱 as Qin; 溱 is Zhen, distinct from 秦.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以復溱、播，等州降德音于梓夔路

decisions.reason: 聖孝 romanizes as Shengxiao; Shengsiao is a corrupted spelling of the same two characters.
尚書省 is the Department of State Affairs; the Secretariat is 中書省.
幸尚書省 is a visit to the Department of State Affairs, not the Secretariat.
定王桓 is Huan, Prince of Ding; the original English fuses title and given name as Ding Huan.
Literal English likewise fuses 定王桓 as Prince of Ding Huan rather than Huan, Prince of Ding.
嗣濮王仲增 is Zhongzeng, holder of the heir-of-Pu princely title, not a fused name Pu Zhongzeng.
The literal line has the same fused title-plus-name; 仲增 is the personal name after the title 嗣濮王.
子楧 is the son Ying; 楧 is not 桓 (Huan), the heir apparent named in s0133.
Literal English repeats Huan for 楧; the graph and pinyin are Ying.
相國公 is a state-dukedom of Xiang, parallel to Duke of Hui for 惠國公. Duke of Xiang is accurate; Xiangguo would echo the office 相國.
The idiomatic line omits 太宰 and 少宰, which the Chinese records beside 少保/特進 and the vice-directorships.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以鄭居中為少保、太宰兼門下侍郎，劉正夫為特進、少宰兼中書侍郎

decisions.reason: 宗粹 is Zongcui; Zongcu drops the final syllable of 粹.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以宗粹為開府儀同三司

decisions.after: On xinwei, He Zhizhong was made Grand Tutor and retired, attending court on the new and full moons.
decisions.reason: 為太傅致仕 grants the rank of Grand Tutor (太傅) upon retirement; Grand Preceptor would be 太師. 朝朔望 is court attendance on new and full moons.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以何執中為太傅致仕，朝朔望

decisions.after: Seventh month, renchen: Xihe, Huanqing, and Jingyuan were shaken by earthquake.
decisions.reason: 環慶 is Huanqing, not Huancqing. The proposal left 熙河 as Xinghe; 熙河 is Xihe (興 would be Xing).

decisions.after: Autumn, seventh month, day renchen: Xihe, Huanqing, and Jingyuan circuits were shaken by earthquake.
decisions.reason: Literal English repeats Huancqing for 環慶 and Xinghe for 熙河; the circuits are Xihe, Huanqing, and Jingyuan.
嘉王楷 is Kai, Prince of Jia, not a personal name Jia Kai; 王 is the title and 楷 the given name.
The literal line likewise fuses 嘉王楷 as Prince of Jia Kai rather than Kai, Prince of Jia.
節度觀察留後 are the acting posts of military and observation commissioners, retitled 承宣使, commissioners for proclaiming orders, not vague commissioner envoys.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 改節度觀察留後為承宣使

decisions.reason: 鄆王 is Prince of Yun (鄆); Yan would be 燕 or 兗.
鄆王 is Prince of Yun, not Yan.
恭帝后 is the posterity of Later Zhou Emperor Gong, not a former empress; 宣義郎 is a male civil rank.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 復立恭帝后以為宣義郎

decisions.reason: 恭帝后 names descendants of Emperor Gong; 后 here is posterity, not empress.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 復立恭帝后以為宣義郎

decisions.reason: 上書人 is a person who submitted a memorial; heterodox is not in the Chinese, and the accent on Yaochén is unnecessary.

claimRetractions.reason: Accepted r0019 shows Zongcu exists only as a truncated romanization of 宗粹; no separate alias is in the Chinese.
Accepted r0023 shows the fused personal name Prince of Jia Kai was created only by the bad English; given name and title are already claimed separately.

claimRevisions.reason: Revised r0001 shows 定國公 is a ducal title (公), not prince (王); the English title must be Duke of Dingguo.
The same repair restores 定國公 as a dukedom held, not a princely title.
Accepted r0015 shows English Huan was produced only by confusing 楧 with 桓; the given name is Ying.
The kinship label must follow the restored given name Ying for 子楧.
Revised r0020 shows 太傅 is Grand Tutor; Grand Preceptor would be 太師. He received that rank on retirement.

value.action: granted He Zhizhong retirement as Grand Preceptor
granted He Zhizhong retirement as Grand Tutor

claimRevisions.reason: The emperor’s grant is retirement with Grand Tutor rank, matching 太傅致仕.
Accepted r0030 restores the unaccented English name An Yaochen for 安堯臣; the accented form came from the translation.
